extracted.intended_audience: researchers and practitioners studying news curation, algorithmic recommendation, and media auditing (e.g., HCI, CS, communication/media studies)
extracted.subtask_description: A case-study style audit of Apple News comparing algorithmically curated (Trending Stories) and human-curated (Top Stories) sections using crowdsourced, sock-puppet, and longitudinal data-collection methods to characterize personalization, geographic adaptation, source diversity, and topic mix.

rubrics_metrics.name: Algorithmic vs editorial distinction (Trending Stories vs Top Stories)
rubrics_metrics.description: Differentiate between Trending Stories (algorithmically curated) and Top Stories (human-curated) when evaluating news curation; comparisons should treat these as distinct pipelines.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The paper focuses on comparing the two sections directly (e.g., via content and mechanism analyses) because they represent algorithmic and human editorial logic respectively.

rubrics_metrics.name: Content personalization (degree of personalization)
rubrics_metrics.description: Measure the extent to which content is personalized to individual users (e.g., minimal, moderate, or extensive personalization).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A crowdsourced audit in this study showed minimal content personalization in the Trending Stories section; personalization can be tested via distributed user accounts or crowd participants.

rubrics_metrics.name: Location-based content adaptation
rubrics_metrics.description: Assess whether the system tailors content based on user geographic location (presence/absence and degree of location adaptation).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This study used a sock-puppet audit and found no location-based content adaptation; sock-puppet or simulated-location accounts are suggested methods to test this dimension.

rubrics_metrics.name: Source diversity
rubrics_metrics.description: Evaluate how many different news sources are surfaced and how varied those sources are within a section or over time.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Measured in the study as one of the comparative metrics between Top Stories and Trending Stories; higher source diversity indicates less dominance by a few outlets.

rubrics_metrics.name: Source concentration
rubrics_metrics.description: Assess the degree to which a small number of sources dominate the presented content (i.e., concentration of sources).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used alongside diversity and evenness to quantify distributional characteristics of sources; lower concentration implies more distributed sourcing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evenness (distributional evenness of sources)
rubrics_metrics.description: Measure how evenly attention or items are distributed across different sources (complements diversity and concentration metrics).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evenness is treated as a separate comparative measure in the study to capture distributional balance among sources.

rubrics_metrics.name: Topic mix / content type (soft news vs hard news)
rubrics_metrics.description: Characterize the topical composition of surfaced stories (e.g., prevalence of 'soft news' such as celebrity/entertainment vs policy and international events).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The study found algorithmic curation featured more 'soft news' about celebrities and entertainment, while editorial curation featured more news about policy and international events; topic coding or content categorization is the suggested approach.

rubrics_metrics.name: Empirical audit methods (crowdsourced audit)
rubrics_metrics.description: Use crowdsourced participants to observe and report what different users see to test personalization and variance across accounts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The paper employed a crowdsourced audit to assess personalization in Trending Stories; guidance implies distributed human observers as a method for detecting user-level variation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Empirical audit methods (sock-puppet audit)
rubrics_metrics.description: Use controlled fake or simulated accounts (sock-puppets) to probe system behaviors like location adaptation or differential treatment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The sock-puppet audit in this study showed no location-based content adaptation; sock-puppet audits are recommended for controlled experiments on system inputs (e.g., location, profile).

rubrics_metrics.name: Longitudinal data collection for comparison
rubrics_metrics.description: Collect data over an extended period (e.g., two months) to compare sections across time and measure consistency, diversity, and concentration longitudinally.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This study used an extended two-month data collection to compare Top Stories and Trending Stories; longitudinal sampling helps capture temporal dynamics and stability of curation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assessment of social, political, and economic implications (gatekeeping power)
rubrics_metrics.description: Evaluate the broader socio-political and economic consequences of the curation system, including its gatekeeping power in the media ecosystem.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The paper frames Apple News as a sociotechnical system exercising gatekeeping power and examines implications of both mechanisms and presented content; audits should therefore include discussion of downstream impacts, not just technical metrics.
